title: Book 6 — Erato, Chapter 132
paragraphs: After the victory at Marathon, Miltiades, who had already stood well with the Athenians, rose to much greater honor. He asked the Athenians for seventy ships, an army, and funds for a campaign, without telling them against what land he meant to go, saying only that he would make them rich if they would go with him, for he would lead them to a country from which they would easily bring back gold in abundance. On this pretext he asked for the ships, and the Athenians, elated by his words, handed them over to him.
